_meta.judge: blind methodological comparison, 11 topics (8 binary + 3 continuous mean-difference), repo C:/meta-harness
_meta.doc_a: our page: C:/meta-harness/docs/reviews/<slug>/index.html, <script>/<style> removed, tags stripped (<[^>]+>), HTML entities unescaped, whitespace collapsed
_meta.order_rule: ord(slug[0]) % 2 == 0 -> ours shown FIRST (balanced, finerenone, pcsk9, denosumab); odd -> ours shown SECOND (colchicine, glp1, omega3, spironolactone). Deterministic from the slug, not random; recorded so it can be re-derived.
_meta.blinding_caveat: Presentation order was blinded but the documents self-identify by genre (one is a harness page that says 'Reproducible meta-analysis harness', the other reads as a journal article). Dimension judgements were made strictly on document content; the reader should treat 'blind' as 'order-blinded', not 'identity-blinded'.
_meta.structural_caveat_for_comparators: The comparator files are text-only extractions. Forest plots (per-trial event counts / effect sizes), RoB summary figures and supplementary tables are referenced but NOT present in the judged document. This structurally lowers comparator scores on 'per-number traceability' and 'risk-of-bias reporting' relative to what the published article shows a reader who has the PDF. Scores below are 'what is IN the judged text', as instructed.
recurring_findings_against_ours: RoB table covers only a subset of the pooled trials: balanced 4/5 pooled trials shown (SPLIT 26444692 missing), colchicine 3/5 (29237033, 27502857 missing), finerenone 1/2 (FIDELIO 33264825 missing), omega3 6/8 (20929341, 38184150 missing), spironolactone 1/2 (RALES 10471456 missing). The page text does not say why these rows are absent.
'Trial integrity: none of the N pooled trials is retracted' uses an N that does not equal k on 4 pages: balanced N=3 vs k=5; colchicine N=4 vs k=5; finerenone N=1 vs k=2; omega3 N=7 vs k=8.

Mixed estimands pooled on one log scale and labelled 'mixed (HR/RR)' or 'mixed (HR/IRR/RR)': finerenone (FIDELIO as count-derived RR + FIGARO as HR), omega3, spironolactone (RALES RR + EMPHASIS HR). Declared, but a reader cannot audit a single named estimand.

omega3 page states three different comparator k values: Comparator tab 'k in the comparator 8', Reproducibility tab 'comparator k = 15 - GAP', and 'comparator pooled 22 for MACE'. The comparator text itself says 22 RCTs for MACE (28 overall).

Search strings on glp1, spironolactone and (partly) denosumab/pcsk9 are PMID [uid] lists or exact-title lookups of already-known trials. They are verbatim and re-runnable (reproducible) but cannot discover trials the author did not already name; the pages' own protocol text says 'exact-title sweeps' / 'UID-anchored queries'. Judged as reproducible but flagged as not a discovery search.
denosumab page labels nonvertebral and hip fracture rows 'Estimand RR' and prints '0.8 (RR)' / '0.6 (RR)' beside a source span that is a hazard ratio.
recurring_findings_against_comparators: Per-trial inputs live in forest plots / Table 1 / supplements; the text gives pooled numbers only (balanced, colchicine, finerenone, glp1, omega3, pcsk9, spironolactone, denosumab all).
Exclusions are aggregate counts in a flow diagram, never per-record with reasons (all 8).

Search strategies are keyword lists or 'available in Supplementary Appendix / on request' rather than verbatim Boolean strings (all 8; finerenone, pcsk9, denosumab say the full strategy is in a supplement).

Internal inconsistencies: finerenone comparator reports renal composite HR 0.86 in Results and 0.84 in Discussion, and a hyperkalaemia CI of 1.93-2.24 around a point of 2.22; spironolactone comparator labels EPHESUS and EMPHASIS-HF as 'HFpEF' with LVEF <=40% in Table 1, says the search was confined to HFmrEF/HFpEF yet pools HFrEF trials, and gives hypotension CI 1.15-1.47 in text vs 1.25-1.47 in the figure legend; colchicine comparator says DerSimonian-Laird random effects if I2>=50 else fixed, then 'combined by fixed-effects'; omega3 comparator's Table 1 reference numbers are offset by one from the citation range [24-51].
_meta.continuous_addendum: esketamine-trd-madrs, melatonin-primary-insomnia-sol, semaglutide-obesity-weight judged in a later pass, same 6-dimension schema, order-blinded by ord(slug[0])%2 (all three odd -> ours shown second); comparator docs are the cached OA full texts.

search_reproducibility.reason: First prints re-runnable query strings ('(Balanced Crystalloids[Title] AND Saline[Title] AND Critically Ill Adults[Title] AND 2018[dp] ...)', CT.gov {cond, intr}) plus a committed cache path and run date; second names databases and a date ('PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov, and Cochrane library from inception through March 01, 2018') but says the search 'was archived through Mendeley program and is available on request'.

per_number_source_traceability.reason: First gives arm counts with a verbatim source sentence per trial ('530 of 2433 patients (21.8%) in the BMES group and in 530 of 2413 patients (22.0%) in the saline group'); second's per-trial event counts are only in Fig. 3/Fig. 4 forest plots, which are not in the text; Table 1 gives arm sizes only.

completeness_of_evidence.reason: For mortality both pool 5 trials (first: PLUS, BaSICS, SMART, SALT, SPLIT; second: Young 2015, Verma, SMART, SALT, Young 2014), but second pools AKI over ~5 trials (18,337 patients) and new RRT over ~5, where first has AKI k=1 and RRT k=2 and declares Verma 2016 and Young 2014 absent for mortality because the abstract lacks counts. First's set carries far more patients (PLUS+BaSICS); second's set is more complete per outcome.

risk_of_bias_reporting.reason: First shows domain-level judgements in the text for 4 trials (D3 'not assessed' declared), but omits SPLIT 26444692 although it is pooled; second applied the full Cochrane tool to all but Ratanarat yet the judgements exist only as 'Quality assessment results are shown in Fig. 2' - none are in the text.

X2 wrong population: title/conditions mention children') and lists each declared-absent trial per outcome with a reason; second reports 'Forty studies were excluded due to lack of outcome of interest' in aggregate.

overall_auditability.reason: A reader can re-run first's queries, open each PMID, and check each pooled count against the quoted sentence; second's inputs require the forest-plot figures and the authors' Mendeley archive. Deductions against first: the retraction line says '3 pooled trials' while k=5, and the RoB table lists 4 of 5 pooled trials.

comparator_stronger_on: Harms completeness: AKI pooled over ~5 trials vs k=1; new RRT over ~5 vs k=2; ICU mortality outcome reported (absent in ours)
Full-text extraction: Verma 2016 and Young 2014 pooled where ours declares them absent from the abstract; Ratanarat 2017 not in our corpus at all
Human risk-of-bias assessment with all seven Cochrane domains (in a figure) and three independent human reviewers with a fourth adjudicator
Broader search reach: 1124 electronic + 21 hand-searched records, Cochrane Library and reference lists, vs 29 records from PubMed/CT.gov
balanced-crystalloids-vs-saline-mortalit.verdict: First (ours) is materially more auditable: verbatim queries, per-number quoted spans, per-record exclusion reasons, per-outcome declared absences. Second (comparator) is the more complete synthesis for harms and uses full-text extraction and human RoB; on mortality the two are at parity in k with disjoint modern trials on our side. Ours has two self-consistency defects a reader would catch (retraction N=3 vs k=5; RoB table missing SPLIT).

Deduction against first: it calls all 9 trials 'blinded and placebo-controlled' while second quotes END-AF's abstract as 'no-colchicine group', an open control.

Full seven-domain Cochrane RoB with a per-domain narrative in the text, plus GRADE (moderate) and a funnel plot
Prospective registration (INPLASY202190004)

The pooled estimates disagree in direction of significance (0.62 significant vs 0.82 non-significant), driven by ours excluding post-PVI and open-control trials and adding COP-AF; a reader can trace why on our page, not on theirs.

_summary.honest_reading: Ours wins auditability on all 8 topics and loses completeness on all 8. The comparators are registered (5 of 8: colchicine INPLASY; finerenone, pcsk9, spironolactone, denosumab PROSPERO), run genuine multi-database searches, and pool 1.1x to 55x more trials. Ours' pages carry self-consistency defects that an auditor would flag (subset RoB tables, retraction-line N != k, mixed estimands, three comparator-k values on the omega3 page, RR/HR label on denosumab secondary rows, 'PARITY' labels on pcsk9 and spironolactone where the comparator pooled 12 and 3 trials respectively).

semaglutide-obesity-weight.verdict: Second (ours) is more auditable because it enforces and documents a single Week-68, treatment-policy mean-difference estimand and exposes each source row and refusal.
